title: Understanding the Logistic Regression Model
text: In logistic regression, the decision boundary is determined by the equation of the form: \( \hat{\beta}_1*x_1 + \hat{\beta}_2*x_2 $$=$$ \log(T/(1-T)) \). Here, \( T \) is the threshold, and \( \hat{\beta} \) are the coefficients.

title: Relating the Decision Boundary to the Line Equation
text: The decision boundary can be rewritten in the form of a line equation: \( $$x_2$$ $$=$$ $$m x_1$$ + $$b$$ \). Here, \( $$m$$ \) is the slope and \( $$b$$ \) is the y-intercept.

title: Finding the Value of \( $$b$$ \)
text: Given the equation \( $$2x_1$$ + $$3x_2$$ $$=$$ \log(3) \), rearrange it to find \( $$b$$ \) in the form \( $$x_2$$ $$=$$ $$m x_1$$ + $$b$$ \).
